# Running One Complete Study {#sec-running-the-loop}

::: {.callout-crux}
What can an architect conclude when the declared Lighthouse cache study cannot
run and a separate retained array study also stops short of the system goal?
:::

The Lighthouse asks for a low-power, 64-bit RISC-V-based compute subsystem for
a real-time mobile extended reality (XR) workload. The lifecycle,
representation, methods, environments, and feedback treatments narrow that
goal to one pre-RTL cache-capacity decision named `XR-L2-CAP-A`
(@sec-architecture-20-ontology; @sec-data-representations-world-models;
@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization;
@sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces;
@sec-feedback-verification-trust). The plan is detailed enough to state
exactly what should run, what should return, and what decision the evidence
could support. The repository does not contain the cache implementation and
measurement path needed to execute it.

That absence is the primary result of this chapter. The prospective cache
study `XR-L2-CAP-A` was not run. No cache number, failure, retry, dispatch,
return, or cost in the author-constructed teaching records is measured project
evidence. The larger cache candidates remain unevaluated, the baseline remains
unrerun, and the pre-RTL decision remains open.

A separate systolic-array study does contain retained inputs and SCALE-Sim
outputs. It appears only after the cache disposition because it answers a
different local question. Its twelve simulator evaluation events preserve a
tie against a weak heuristic, a failed directional explanation, incomplete
provenance, and a pending architecture handoff. The array record shows what an
executed but limited study can establish. It cannot complete the cache study,
validate the 3\ W subsystem target, or stand in for the Lighthouse system.

The XR cache remains the primary Lighthouse thread, while the secondary array
case is the complete bounded study carried through execution to an honest
technical stop. Neither case is a complete Lighthouse success.

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}
After reading this chapter, you can:

- Trace the Lighthouse goal to the exact cache candidates, fixed state, tool
  requests, checks, budget, and intended pre-RTL decision in `XR-L2-CAP-A`.
- Distinguish specification identities and author-constructed teaching
  records from retained execution evidence.
- Report architecture outcome, AI contribution, mechanism status, and
  stopping as separate judgments when a study never reaches execution.
- Interpret the retained array chronology, local measurements, provenance
  gaps, proposal overlap, failed explanation, and pending handoff without
  widening its claims.
- Explain why exhaustive enumeration is the missing conventional comparator
  for a newly frozen array study and identify the system questions that still
  block a Lighthouse conclusion.

:::

## From the Lighthouse Goal to One Cache Decision

The primary study begins with one architecture decision rather than an AI
method. The system goal is the 3\ W XR compute subsystem introduced in
@sec-moonshot. The local question asks which, if either, of two larger L2
capacities should advance to RTL evaluation against the current smaller
capacity. The represented study is `XR-L2-CAP-A`. Its declared cache plan fixes
the comparison against the 2\ MB baseline, design revision `XR-COMPUTE-A`, and
run specification `RUN-SPEC-A`.

The candidate identities are `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, and `L2-4M-A`.
`L2-2M-A` is the specified baseline, while `L2-3M-A` and `L2-4M-A` are the
specified alternatives. These names identify objects in the prospective
study. They are not retained cache configurations, generated instances, or
measured artifacts in this repository.

The represented field `l2.capacity` admits exactly the tokens `2MB`, `3MB`,
and `4MB`. Those tokens identify the three specification choices. They do not
resolve the byte unit conflict that appears later in the declared tool
interface.

Only `l2.capacity` may change. The plan fixes cache policy `CACHE-POLICY-A`,
network-on-chip configuration `NOC-A`, memory-system configuration `MEMSYS-A`,
the 2\ GHz microarchitecture, compiler `COMPILER-A`, runtime `RUNTIME-A`,
RISC-V software image `SW-BASE-A`, and workload snapshot `XR-TRACE-A` with
stable frame identifiers and boundaries. It also fixes the identities of the
planned cycle-level simulator `SIM-A`, cache model `CACHE-A`, power model
`PM-A`, SRAM model `SRAM-A`, and process, voltage, and temperature assumptions
`PVT-A`.

The architecture claim is that a larger L2 could reduce 99th-percentile frame
time by removing capacity misses while satisfying the declared power, area,
access-time, functional, and coherence checks. A reduction in misses alone
would not establish the claim. The matched frame observations would have to
show that the reduction reaches the tail-latency outcome under the fixed
workload and software state.

The legal set contains only the baseline and two alternatives. Direct
evaluation was therefore selected in @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization.
The prospective study adds no generator, predictor, optimizer, or learned
search method. `SRAM-A` is part of the declared tool path, not a newly selected
AI component. This choice leaves no AI-contribution claim to test in the cache
study. It simply chooses the smallest approach that could answer the declared
architecture question if the tool path existed.

The intended result is also narrow. The study could recommend at most one
capacity for a later RTL study. It could not authorize implementation,
signoff, tapeout, or a product commitment. Cache policy, prefetching,
coherence, network-on-chip changes, compiler changes, software scheduling,
full floorplanning, thermal signoff, resistive voltage-drop review, security,
reliability, and product cost remain outside the study.

## The Declared Cache Run

The preceding chapters collectively specify the planned work. The compact
request in @tbl-cache-run-declaration preserves the exact tool roles, required
returns, checks, budget, and stopping conditions without treating any of them
as completed.

| **Run field** | **Declared `XR-L2-CAP-A` work** |
| --- | --- |
| **Candidate requests** | Prepare one complete `SRAM-A` request under `PVT-A` for each of `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, and `L2-4M-A`. Preserve capacity, geometry, banking, ports, modeled periphery, SRAM-model identity, and technology identity. Only `l2.capacity` may vary. |
| **Cycle-level requests** | Rerun the `L2-2M-A` baseline and run eligible alternatives through `SIM-A` with `CACHE-A` and `PM-A` under the same `XR-TRACE-A`, `SW-BASE-A`, and fixed hardware and software identities. |
| **Dispatch condition** | A cycle-level request is eligible only when `(return_complete == true) && (schema_valid == true) && (area_mm2 <= 1.5) && (access_time_ns <= 2.5)`. This condition authorizes a request. It does not by itself validate a measurement or reject an architecture candidate. |
| **Required returns** | Retain SRAM area, access time, cache-local energy and leakage, matched frame records and frame-time inputs, 99th-percentile frame time, cache misses by classification, subsystem dynamic plus leakage power, tool and model identities, translated inputs, warnings, failures, hashes, lineage, and realized cost. |
| **Checks** | Require identical ISA-visible outputs for the declared tests, the same functional regression suite for every capacity, no failure from the simulator's coherence-invariant checks, modeled subsystem dynamic plus leakage power at or below 3\ W, cache macro area at or below 1.5\ mm^2^, modeled access time at or below 2.5\ ns, and an uncertainty-qualified frame-time comparison against the rerun baseline. Thermal and IR-drop review remain independent later requirements. |
| **Failure handling** | Refuse an invalid request before invocation. Keep timeouts, cancellations, infrastructure failures, stale state, missing output, and parser failures distinct. An authorized retry must link to its parent, consume the cycle-level budget, and begin from regenerated clean state without changing the candidate. |
| **Budget** | Allow three SRAM evaluations and at most four cycle-level executions in total, including infrastructure reruns. No RTL synthesis or physical signoff is included. |
| **Stopping** | Stop an attempt when its queue-wait or run-time deadline expires. Stop the study when the intended decision is resolved, all eligible capacities are exhausted, the cycle-level budget is spent, the absolute deadline expires, a required input or tool remains unavailable, or no alternative passes the SRAM limits. |
| **Decision** | Recommend at most one capacity for later RTL evaluation only when its required checks pass and its qualified frame-time comparison against the rerun baseline remains above zero. |

: **The declaration specifies a cache run without creating one.** It fixes the
requests, returns, checks, budget, and intended decision that a later execution
would have to satisfy. {#tbl-cache-run-declaration tbl-colwidths="[22,78]"}

The placeholder names in the declaration preserve study roles and identities.
The repository does not bind `SRAM-A`, `SIM-A`, `CACHE-A`, or `PM-A` to an
installed tool, executable, configuration, or retained output. Mapping those
names to familiar cache, simulator, or power tools would invent an
implementation path that the study does not retain.

The capacity unit also needs repair before execution. The earlier study,
representation, and method declarations describe the alternatives as 2, 3,
and 4\ MB (@sec-architecture-20-ontology;
@sec-data-representations-world-models;
@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). The later environment
request schema instead defines the serialized values as integer counts of
mebibytes (MiB), where 1\ MiB is $2^{20}$ bytes
(@sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces). MB and MiB are not
interchangeable units. The candidate identities remain stable specification
names, but a new executable contract must choose one unit, state the byte
count, and regenerate every dependent request before any comparison begins.

Nothing in @tbl-cache-run-declaration was materialized or executed for this
book. No functional regression, coherence check, tail-latency comparison,
power check, area check, access-time check, thermal review, or IR-drop review
produced cache evidence.

## What the Repository Actually Retains

The cache material falls into three evidence classes. Specification identities
state what a study intends to compare. Author-constructed teaching records
show what an execution record could look like. Executed evidence would require
retained requests, outputs, statuses, and lineage from an actual run. The
repository retains the first two classes and no executed cache evidence.

The compact inventory in @tbl-cache-evidence-inventory keeps those classes
separate.

| **Retained item** | **Evidence class** | **What it supports** | **What remains absent** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `XR-L2-CAP-A` and its declared cache plan | Specification identity | The cache question, comparator, scope, constraints, measurements, budget, stopping conditions, and intended pre-RTL decision. | Executable requests, runs, measurements, and a cache disposition. |
| `XR-COMPUTE-A`, fixed-state identifiers, and `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, `L2-4M-A` | Specification identity | The intended design revision, invariant state, permitted capacity field, and candidate mapping. | Retained candidate files, generated cache instances, regeneration evidence, and implementation collateral. |
| `RUN-SPEC-A` and its placeholder tool identities | Specification identity | The intended request translation, dispatch condition, return schema, failure handling, budget, and tool responsibilities. | Bound executables, wrapper and parser versions, exact inputs, host state, commands, logs, outputs, and realized cost. |
| `SRAM-2-A1`, `SRAM-3-A1`, and `SRAM-4-A1` | Author-constructed teaching record | Illustrative area and access-time pairs of 1.2\ mm^2^ and 2.1\ ns, 1.4\ mm^2^ and 2.4\ ns, and 1.7\ mm^2^ and 2.8\ ns. | Terminal and parser status, serialized inputs, raw artifacts, energy, leakage, exact dispatch evidence, and any measured result. |
| `SIM-2-A1`, `SIM-3-A1`, `SIM-3-A2`, `SIM-3-A3`, and `SIM-3-SUMMARY-A` | Author-constructed teaching record | An illustrative baseline power indication of 2.90\ W, one stated stale-state setup failure, two indicated returns with no values, and one indicated derived summary. | Evidence that any request was dispatched, failed, retried, returned, parsed, compared, or consumed budget. |
| Lifecycle design-card figure | Author-constructed teaching fixture | A compact illustration of fields that a study record might index. | A retained cache run or evidence that its displayed entries occurred. The fixture is not merged into the cache evidence. |
| Retained cache execution package | Executed evidence | None. No such package is present. | Candidate artifacts, tool requests, raw outputs, parsed measurements, hashes, lineage, costs, qualified comparisons, and a decision record. |

: **The repository retains a cache specification and teaching fixtures, not a
cache experiment.** Similar-looking identifiers across chapters do not convert
constructed entries into executed evidence. {#tbl-cache-evidence-inventory tbl-colwidths="[22,18,28,32]"}

The constructed values are useful only for teaching how missing fields remain
visible. None of the numbers, failures, retries, dispatches, returns, or costs
in that fixture happened in a retained cache run. The table's statement that no
4\ MB simulator request appears does not verify that `L2-4M-A` was rejected or
that a complete dispatch check withheld the request. The illustrative area and
access-time pair cannot supply that missing status.

The same boundary applies to `L2-3M-A`. The constructed teaching record does
not establish that the candidate was measured, feasible, faster than the
baseline, or compliant with the 3\ W limit. Its indicated later returns have
no values, artifacts, state identities, parser status, or lineage. The
baseline entry similarly does not establish that `L2-2M-A` was rerun under
matched conditions or qualified for comparison.

The candidate and tool names therefore remain specification identities. They
should not be searched for as if they named retained cache files, and familiar
real tools should not be substituted for the placeholders. The absent
implementation path is the fact that controls the next decision.

## The Unresolved Cache Decision

A study that stops before execution still needs separate judgments. The four
judgments in @tbl-cache-judgments prevent an empty run from acquiring a result
through narrative completion.

| **Judgment** | **Cache conclusion** | **Evidence boundary** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Architecture outcome** | Unresolved. No capacity advances, and none is rejected. | No retained cache candidate was executed, the baseline was not rerun, and no required comparison was qualified. |
| **AI contribution** | Not tested. | Direct evaluation with no added learned method was the declared approach. No AI-versus-conventional comparison exists. |
| **Mechanism** | Untested. | No retained miss classifications or matched frame observations test whether reduced capacity misses change 99th-percentile frame time. |
| **Stopping** | Stop before execution because the implementation and measurement path is unavailable. | The declared budget was not consumed. The next action is a new, fully retained run after the unit, candidate artifacts, tool bindings, request translation, and measurement path are made executable. |

: **The cache decision remains open for four different reasons.** Missing
execution leaves the architecture outcome unresolved, the declared no-added-method
choice leaves AI contribution untested, missing observations leave the mechanism
untested, and the absent tool path fixes the stopping point. {#tbl-cache-judgments tbl-colwidths="[18,34,48]"}

The stop belongs before execution. It is not a budget exhaustion, a failed
candidate, or a no-change architecture result. It does not authorize
`L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, or `L2-4M-A` for RTL work. The only supported next move
is to begin a new run whose retained package contains the exact candidate
artifacts, resolved byte units, bound tools, translated inputs, raw and parsed
returns, realized costs, qualified comparison, and accountable decision.

## A Secondary Executed Array Case {#sec-executed-scale-study}

The repository also retains a different study named
`arch2_scale_ai_study_v1`. The [archived v0.1.7 package](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/v0.1.7/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study)
retains its preregistration, model and execution provenance, results, and
manifest. It evaluates systolic-array shapes for three
synthetic general matrix multiplication (GEMM) layers. Their (M, N, K)
dimensions are 128 by 128 by 256, 64 by 192 by 128, and 32 by 128 by 192. The
local architecture purpose is to compare systolic-array geometries under one
fixed workload and simulator configuration. The layers are not traces from an
identified spatial-tracking pipeline or a complete XR application.

This secondary case changes only array height and width under a fixed
SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 configuration with weight-stationary dataflow, 128\ KiB each
for the three SRAMs, and configured interface bandwidth fields of 64 words per
cycle [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The retained protocol uses a
1,024-processing-element legality limit, a
90,000-cycle cutoff, a mandatory 32 by 32 baseline, four simulator evaluation
events per proposal arm, and four shared mechanism-probe events. The recorded
800\ MHz clock is used only for derived latency. The chapter's judgments use
cycles.

The retained record does not justify using the fixed heuristic instead of
exhaustive enumeration. The missing exhaustive comparator is a documented
design limitation of the frozen study, not an outcome that can be repaired
retroactively.

The local lower-is-better score is

$$
S = \frac{\text{total cycles}}
         {\text{average layer utilization}/100}.
$$

The runner computes this score from retained SCALE-Sim outputs. It is not a
physical measurement, an area-delay product, or a universal accelerator
metric. The runner sums the `Total Cycles` column and excludes the separate
prefetch-inclusive column. Average layer utilization is the arithmetic mean of
the three per-layer SCALE-Sim `Overall Util %` values, not `Compute Util %`, so
each layer has equal weight. The score does not explicitly price
processing-element count, area, or modeled memory traffic.

The retained records also show how the comparison was constructed. Both arms
receive the same three-row CSV workload, which records a layer name and the M,
N, and K dimensions for each dense GEMM. Array rows and columns must come from
the set 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128, their product must not exceed 1,024 processing
elements, and the runner inserts the mandatory 32 by 32 baseline. Every
candidate runs under the same workload, layout, SCALE-Sim configuration,
dataflow, SRAM capacities, bandwidth fields, deadline, checks, and local
score.

The model's permitted role is equally narrow. It may return three unique legal
nonbaseline shapes and a mechanism hypothesis. It cannot invoke SCALE-Sim,
waive a check, choose the recommendation, or make the architecture decision.
The deterministic heuristic excludes the baseline and orders every legal
shape first by decreasing processing-element count, then by the absolute
log2 distance between the shape's columns-to-rows ratio and the aggregate
workload N-to-M ratio, and finally by increasing row count and column count.
It selects the first three shapes in that order.

The inserted baseline gives each proposal arm four simulator events. This is
equal simulator-event allocation, not equal total effort. The study does not
equate those events with model inference, prompt development, heuristic
construction, human setup, or review cost.

### The Retained Chronology

The actual record contains one setup failure before inference, one valid model
call, and twelve successful simulator evaluation records. The chronology in
@tbl-array-chronology reports only fields retained in the package.

| **Recorded event** | **Action and return** | **Retained support and limit** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Freeze, 2026-07-14 18:19:48 UTC** | The preregistration records the workload, legal shapes, heuristic candidates, score, margin, budgets, rejection checks, mechanism contrast, and decision boundary. | An internal timestamp records this order. No external timestamp or commit binding independently proves precedence. |
| **Rejected schema request, 18:21:00 UTC** | The response-format service rejects the original JSON Schema before inference because two constant-string properties lack explicit types. No model output or usage is produced. | The old and new schema hashes and a prose error description are retained. The rejected schema body and service response are not retained, so semantic equivalence of the amendment cannot be independently checked. |
| **Schema amendment, 18:21:41 UTC** | The record adds explicit types and marks the change non-substantive. | The package records the amendment before inference but does not retain both schema bodies. |
| **Proposal call, 18:21:51–18:22:24 UTC** | One valid call returns 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 32 by 16 plus a directional mechanism prediction. No repair call follows. | The full response, 32.90 seconds of wall time, and token usage are retained. Provider revision, seed, temperature, top-p, host runtime, currency cost, and an exact matching prompt copy are unavailable. |
| **Simulator window, 18:31:23–18:31:42 UTC** | The record contains eight proposal-arm evaluation events and four shared mechanism-probe events. All twelve carry `status: ok`; both declared checks pass in every record. | The aggregate runner window is 19.05 seconds. Per-evaluation timestamps, commands, exit codes, logs, queue time, resource use, and human effort are not retained. No invalid-candidate, rejection, timeout, retry, or simulator-recovery path is exercised. |
| **Technical stop and handoff** | No evaluated nonbaseline shape clears the one-percent margin. The proposal arms tie, and the predicted winner reversal fails. | The machine-readable recommendation retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stops the bounded search. Its accountable decision status remains `awaiting_author_confirmation`. |

: **The array chronology records what happened and what is missing.** One
schema setup failure precedes a valid model call, twelve simulator events
complete, and the architecture handoff remains pending. {#tbl-array-chronology tbl-colwidths="[20,40,40]"}

The model provenance names OpenAI through Codex CLI 0.144.4 and the requested
alias `gpt-5.4`. It records 13,223 input tokens, including 1,920 cached tokens,
and 1,446 output tokens, including 516 reasoning tokens. Currency cost was not
reported. The exact hosted model revision and sampling identity were not
exposed, so another call cannot be treated as reproduction of this one.

The retained prompt has a second provenance break. The preregistration and
model record name SHA-256 `ec12df200a134532...76fbca`, while the surviving
prompt copy hashes to `36e0167aa338c6b...6971`. The complete response survives,
but the exact context that produced it cannot be verified.

The simulator provenance records macOS 26.4 on arm64, Python 3.11.15,
`arch2_labs` 0.1.0, SCALE-Sim 3.0.0, and a local executable path. It does not
bind the historical runner to a repository commit, dependency lock,
container, or complete host state. The reference manifest covers the retained
reference-output tree, not the preregistration, prompt, model response,
provenance record, runner source, dependency lock, or repository commit as one
sealed identity.

The retained array directory contains no independently preserved validation
receipt artifact. This chapter therefore does not treat reference integrity,
replay, or focused tests as independently verified. The retained files and
current replay path remain inspectable, but replay would still share the
workload, runner, simulator, score, and assumptions of the recorded
computation.

### The Local Results

The model arm evaluates the mandatory baseline plus its three proposals. The
fixed aggregate-aspect-ratio heuristic evaluates the same baseline plus 16 by
64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16. The two arms overlap on two nonbaseline shapes.
Including the repeated baseline, both arms receive four simulator evaluation
events. That equality does not match model inference, human setup, heuristic
construction, prompt development, review effort, or total cost.

The exact proposal-arm results appear in @tbl-array-results. Repeated rows are
separate budget events, not independent measurements.

| **Arm** | **Shape and source** | **Cycles** | **Average layer utilization** | **Local score** | **Result within arm** |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Model | 32 by 32 baseline | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 16 by 64 proposal | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 8 by 128 proposal | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Model | 32 by 16 proposal | 25,277 | 45.438% | 55,629.61 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 32 by 32 baseline | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 16 by 64 proposal | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 8 by 128 proposal | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 64 by 16 proposal | 17,757 | 32.294% | 54,985.25 | Ranked worse |

: **The two proposal arms tie under equal simulator-event budgets.** Neither
finds an evaluated nonbaseline shape that clears the recorded one-percent
margin over 32 by 32. The values come from retained SCALE-Sim outputs and the
runner's local score, not silicon. {#tbl-array-results tbl-colwidths="[12,23,11,18,14,22]"}

The best evaluated nonbaseline, 16 by 64, exactly matches the baseline on
cycles, average layer utilization, and local score. It does not clear the
change margin. The 8 by 128, 32 by 16, and 64 by 16 results rank worse under
the frozen score. This is a no-change outcome for five unique evaluated
shapes. It is not evidence that 32 by 32 is optimal among all legal shapes.

Two panels keep the proposal comparison and the mechanism probe separate
(@fig-ai-study-result).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ai-study-result
#| fig-cap: |
#|   **The local tie and failed mechanism test answer different questions.** The left panel reports every proposal-arm score under equal four-event simulator budgets. The 32 by 32 baseline and 16 by 64 shape tie in both arms. The right panel records that 16 by 64 remains ahead of 64 by 16 after M and N are exchanged, contrary to the predicted reversal. None of the values are measured on silicon.
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel study result. Horizontal bars show all model and fixed heuristic candidate scores, with the baseline and 16 by 64 tied at the lowest score in both arms. A paired-line plot shows 16 by 64 beating 64 by 16 on both the original and transposed workloads, contrary to the predicted reversal."

import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from _python.plots import COLORS, apply_style

apply_style()

result_path = Path("../labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json")
result = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]
probe_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] == "mechanism_probe"]

shape_labels = {
    "model_baseline_32x32": "M  32×32 baseline",
    "ai_wide_16x64": "M  16×64",
    "ai_extreme_8x128": "M  8×128",
    "ai_compact_32x16": "M  32×16",
    "conventional_baseline_32x32": "H  32×32 baseline",
    "heuristic_16x64": "H  16×64",
    "heuristic_8x128": "H  8×128",
    "heuristic_64x16": "H  64×16",
}

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(5.6, 2.65), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.35, 1]})
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.22, right=0.985, top=0.82, bottom=0.18, wspace=0.42)

labels = [shape_labels[r["candidate_id"]] for r in arm_runs]
scores = [r["decision_score"] / 1000 for r in arm_runs]
colors = [COLORS["blue"] if r["arm"] == "model" else COLORS["green"] for r in arm_runs]
y = list(range(len(arm_runs)))
ax1.barh(y, scores, color=colors, height=0.66)
ax1.set_yticks(y, labels)
ax1.invert_yaxis()
ax1.set_xlabel("local score (thousands; lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)
ax1.set_title("Equal-call candidate evaluation", fontsize=7, pad=5)
for yi, score in zip(y, scores):
    ax1.text(score + 0.8, yi, f"{score:.1f}", va="center", fontsize=5.5, color=COLORS["ink"])
ax1.set_xlim(0, max(scores) * 1.18)

probe = {}
for run in probe_runs:
    workload = "transposed" if "transposed" in run["candidate_id"] else "original"
    shape = f'{run["array_rows"]}×{run["array_cols"]}'
    probe[(shape, workload)] = run["decision_score"] / 1000

x = [0, 1]
for shape, color, marker in [("16×64", COLORS["blue"], "o"), ("64×16", COLORS["orange"], "s")]:
    values = [probe[(shape, "original")], probe[(shape, "transposed")]]
    ax2.plot(x, values, marker=marker, markersize=4.2, linewidth=1.5, color=color, label=shape)
    for xi, value in zip(x, values):
        ax2.text(xi, value + 1.1, f"{value:.1f}", ha="center", fontsize=5.5, color=color)

ax2.set_xticks(x, ["original", "M/N transposed"])
ax2.set_ylabel("local score (thousands)", fontsize=6.5)
ax2.set_title("Mechanism probe: no reversal", fontsize=7, pad=5)
ax2.set_ylim(18, 61)
ax2.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=6, loc="upper right")

for ax in (ax1, ax2):
    ax.tick_params(axis="both", labelsize=5.9, length=2.5, width=0.6, pad=2)
    ax.grid(axis="x" if ax is ax1 else "y", color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=0.55, zorder=0)
    for spine in ["top", "right"]:
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["left"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])

plt.show()
```

The tie provides no study-local AI advantage over the weak fixed heuristic.
It also provides no evidence of equal capability, equal total cost, or parity
with exhaustive enumeration, an expert study, a solver, or another search
method. One proposal call supplies no estimate of variation or reliability for
the model family.

The retained results establish equal cycles and average layer utilization for
32 by 32 and 16 by 64 under the frozen score, but they do not establish the
architectural cause of that equality. The following transposition probe tests
a separate mechanism hypothesis by comparing 16 by 64 with 64 by 16.

### The Failed Directional Explanation

The model predicted that 16 by 64 would beat 64 by 16 on the original workload
and that 64 by 16 would win after M and N were exchanged. The original local
scores are 33,782.40 and 54,985.25. The transposed scores are 23,530.65 and
25,458.11. The predicted reversal does not occur. The narrower transposed gap
does not rescue the explanation.

The transposed 16 by 64 input config declares `Bandwidth = 64,64,64`, while
one retained report row gives `Avg OFMAP DRAM BW` as 79.073 words per cycle.
The retained record does not explain the relationship between those fields.
Their bandwidth semantics remain unresolved, and the configured value is not
evidence of a demonstrated physical or shared-system limit.

The surviving prompt copy also omits the mapping semantics needed to interpret
the contrast. The retained execution records identify SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 but no
dependency hash or source commit. The K-height, N-width, and M-temporal
interpretation here follows the tagged v3.0.0 implementation
[@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source]. Under SCALE-Sim's weight-stationary GEMM
mode, array height carries K, array width carries N, and M streams through the array
(@fig-array-mapping). Exchanging M and N leaves K unchanged, while mirroring
16 by 64 and 64 by 16 changes both the N-fold count on width and the K-fold
count on height.

![**The retained contrast does not isolate array orientation.** In the tagged SCALE-Sim v3.0.0 implementation [@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source], weight-stationary GEMM maps K to array height and N to array width, while M streams through the array. Exchanging M and N leaves K unchanged, so the mirrored shapes change more than one fold count.](images/F8-array-mapping){#fig-array-mapping fig-alt="A GEMM workload feeds a resident weight tile of K by N, which maps onto wide 16 by 64 and tall 64 by 16 arrays. K maps over array height and N over array width. A dashed transpose connector notes that K is unchanged, so the mirrored pair changes more than one fold count."}

The directional prediction fails its declared test, but the contrast does not
establish a replacement mechanism. It does not show that orientation is
irrelevant. A new mechanism study would need a prompt with pinned mapping
semantics and a contrast that varies one relevant fold count at a time.

The retained array record therefore ends with four bounded judgments. No
evaluated nonbaseline clears the architecture margin. No local AI advantage is
demonstrated against the weak heuristic. The directional explanation fails
without yielding a replacement. The technical search stops, while the
accountable architecture decision remains pending.

SCALE-Sim establishes none of the physical properties that the Lighthouse
decision needs. It does not measure energy, physical bandwidth, timing, power,
area, thermal behavior, or silicon performance. Its configured bandwidth
fields and reported operand traffic do not describe a verified shared system
interface. The synthetic workload and local array result cannot close the
cache decision, the 3\ W requirement, or the Lighthouse system.

## Exhaustive Enumeration as the Missing Comparator

The array study's legal space is small and closed. It contains exactly fifteen
shapes under the declared dimension set and 1,024-processing-element limit.
The retained proposal-arm evaluations cover five unique shapes, leaving ten
unexecuted. The exact coverage appears in @tbl-array-shape-coverage.

| **Status** | **Exact legal shapes** | **Count** |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Evaluated as unique original-workload geometries | 8 by 128; 16 by 64; 32 by 16; 32 by 32; 64 by 16 | 5 |
| Not executed | 8 by 8; 8 by 16; 8 by 32; 8 by 64; 16 by 8; 16 by 16; 16 by 32; 32 by 8; 64 by 8; 128 by 8 | 10 |

: **Five evaluated geometries do not close a fifteen-shape space.** Repeated
arm events preserve the frozen budgets but add no new geometry. The ten other
legal shapes have no retained SCALE-Sim result. {#tbl-array-shape-coverage tbl-colwidths="[25,62,13]"}

For a newly frozen follow-up study, exhaustive enumeration is the appropriate
primary conventional comparator. It would evaluate every legal shape under
one fixed workload, simulator configuration, score, and set of checks. The
current study did not perform that enumeration. No outcome for the ten
unexecuted shapes can be inferred, and enumeration cannot be added
retroactively to claim that the recorded model tied or beat the complete
space.

The frozen score also omits a reported axis that could matter to a later
system decision. The 16 by 64 shape ties the baseline at 13,917 cycles and
41.196 percent average layer utilization, yet the retained reports contain
409,726 modeled DRAM-word writes for 16 by 64 and 204,863 for 32 by 32. The
64 by 16 shape reports 102,400 modeled writes and fewer total modeled word
accesses than the baseline while taking more cycles. These are simulator
outputs, not identified physical DRAM transactions or energy measurements.

The baseline dominates the shared 16 by 64 candidate on the two reported
quantities of cycles and modeled writes (@fig-proxy-mismatch). This post-run
observation exposes a proxy limitation. It does not change the frozen score,
establish physical memory energy, or authorize a new disposition.

```{python}
#| label: fig-proxy-mismatch
#| fig-cap: |
#|   **The frozen score omits modeled memory traffic.** The local score ranks the shared 16 by 64 candidate exactly equal to the 32 by 32 baseline. Across cycles and modeled DRAM-word writes, the baseline dominates that candidate. This post-run observation does not change the frozen outcome or establish physical memory energy.
#| out-width: "80%"
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of evaluated systolic array shapes using two SCALE-Sim outputs. The 32 by 32 baseline and shared 16 by 64 candidate both take 13,917 cycles, while the shared candidate reports about twice the modeled DRAM-word writes."

import json
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from _python.plots import COLORS, apply_style

apply_style()

result_path = Path("../labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json")
result = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.5))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.18, right=0.95, top=0.88, bottom=0.15)

ax.set_title("Frozen Score Omits Modeled Memory Traffic", fontsize=7.5, pad=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Compute Cycles (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)
ax.set_ylabel("Modeled DRAM-word writes (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)

seen = set()
for r in arm_runs:
    key = (r["workload_id"], r["array_rows"], r["array_cols"])
    if key in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(key)

    cid = r["candidate_id"]
    cycles = r["metrics"]["total_cycles"]
    dram_writes = r["metrics"]["dram_writes"]
    label = cid.replace("model_baseline_", "").replace("ai_wide_", "").replace("ai_extreme_", "").replace("ai_compact_", "").replace("conventional_baseline_", "").replace("heuristic_", "")

    if "32x32" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="o", markersize=5, color=COLORS["blue"])
        ax.text(cycles - 500, dram_writes - 10000, f"Baseline\n{label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="right", va="top")
    elif "16x64" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="X", markersize=5, color=COLORS["red"])
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes + 15000, f"Shared candidate\n{label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="left", va="bottom")
    else:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="s", markersize=4, color=COLORS["orange"], alpha=0.6)
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes, label, color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5, ha="left", va="center", alpha=0.7)

baseline_cycles = next(
    r["metrics"]["total_cycles"]
    for r in arm_runs
    if r["workload_id"] == "original"
    and r["array_rows"] == 32
    and r["array_cols"] == 32
)
ax.axvline(x=baseline_cycles, color=COLORS["grid"], linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)

ax.tick_params(axis="both", labelsize=5.9, length=2.5, width=0.6, pad=2)
ax.grid(True, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=0.55, zorder=0)
for spine in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])

plt.show()
```

A new enumeration study would need to freeze its decision quantities before
execution. It could retain the original local score for comparability, add a
separately justified memory-aware quantity, or replace the score. None of
those choices can rescore the completed record. The unresolved memory axis is
part of the reason that neither exhaustive coverage nor the current local
ranking alone would establish energy, power, or Lighthouse suitability.

## Returning Both Records to the Lighthouse

The cache and array records now return to the same system goal with different
dispositions. The comparison in @tbl-lighthouse-return prevents one record
from filling the other's missing evidence.

| **Record** | **Architecture outcome** | **AI contribution** | **Mechanism** | **Stopping and action** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prospective cache study `XR-L2-CAP-A` | Unresolved. No cache candidate was evaluated, rejected, or advanced. | Not tested because direct evaluation with no added learned method was selected. | Untested. No retained result connects capacity misses to 99th-percentile frame time. | Stop before execution because the cache implementation and measurement path is unavailable. Begin a new fully retained run. |
| Executed array study `arch2_scale_ai_study_v1` | No evaluated nonbaseline clears the local margin for five unique shapes. This is not an optimality result. | No local advantage is demonstrated against the weak heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets. Equal total cost and method parity were not measured. | The directional reversal prediction fails, and no replacement explanation is established. | The local technical search stops. Retaining 32 by 32 for the evaluated set is a pending recommendation, not an authorized architecture change. |

: **The two records stop at different technical boundaries.** The cache study
never executes, while the array study completes a narrow simulator comparison
whose action remains pending. Neither result can close the other.
{#tbl-lighthouse-return tbl-colwidths="[19,22,20,18,21]"}

The executed case shows how each returned result changes the conclusion. The
local question asks which legal array shape should advance for the synthetic
GEMM workload, and the model and deterministic heuristic supply two proposal
procedures. Eight proposal-arm simulator records then return a tie at the
frozen margin, so the evaluated set supports neither an architecture change
nor a local AI advantage. The four mechanism-probe records leave 16 by 64
ahead after transposition instead of reversing the winner, so the proposed
explanation fails without a replacement.
The retained traffic counts then expose a quantity omitted from the frozen
score, which prevents the tied score from supporting an energy or system-level
claim. Those signals justify stopping the recorded search with the 32 by 32
recommendation still awaiting confirmation. They also justify a new exhaustive
comparison across all fifteen legal shapes, followed by the system checks that
SCALE-Sim cannot perform. Neither follow-up ran in this study.

Placing this chronology beside the Lighthouse teaches where the evidence
ends. It does not turn the synthetic array workload into evidence for the
cache question, XR performance, or the 3\ W target.

Both records leave the central system questions open. Neither retains an
identified XR workload trace or validates tail deadlines across deployed
conditions. Neither executes the compiler, runtime, RISC-V interface, host
cores, shared memory path, sensors, or display engine. Neither supplies a
complete verification plan or checks the full subsystem's function, security,
or reliability.

The physical questions also remain. No retained evidence closes timing,
routing, area, power delivery, the 3\ W subsystem budget, thermal behavior, or
silicon performance. The array reports contain modeled local traffic, but no
shared-memory contention or physical energy model connects that traffic to the
Lighthouse platform. The cache plan names some of these checks, but naming a
check is not running it.

The bounded dispositions are therefore plain. The cache architecture decision
is unresolved. The array study reaches a local technical stop, demonstrates no
AI advantage, and leaves its accountable action pending. Neither case is a
complete Lighthouse success.

## Open Research Questions

These records expose three research problems at the boundary between a local
study and a system decision.

**Executing an incomplete study.** Missing tools or observations can stop a
study before its declared comparison begins.

- **How can an AI-assisted architecture study produce a valid bounded result
when part of its required implementation or measurement path is unavailable?**
  A useful method must distinguish claims that can still be tested from those
  that require a new tool path, then quantify the cost and error introduced by
  any substitute observation.

**Choosing a decisive comparison.** Small budgets and overlapping candidates
can make two approaches indistinguishable even when their internal procedures
differ.

- **How can a study predict before execution whether its candidate set,
comparison method, and evaluation budget have enough resolving power?** A
  credible answer should identify likely ties or censored comparisons before
  expensive tool work and remain reliable when evaluation cost varies across
  candidates.

- **How should an AI-assisted design system select the next system-relevant
check when a valid local result cannot support the architecture decision?**
  The open problem is to choose among workload, software, memory, verification,
  and physical checks using their information value, cost, shared assumptions,
  and ability to change the pending decision.

## Conclusion

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Stop at the last retained result"}
Separate the architecture outcome, AI contribution, mechanism, and stopping
decision. When execution evidence ends, leave every downstream claim open and
state the new work required to continue.
:::

The primary cache study reaches an honest stop before execution. Its exact
candidate identities, fixed state, planned requests, required returns, checks,
budget, and intended pre-RTL decision survive. Its implementation and
measurement path does not. The repository therefore supports no cache
measurement, candidate rejection, retry, dispatch, return, cost, baseline
comparison, AI-contribution result, mechanism result, or architecture
recommendation.

The secondary array study reaches a different stop. It retains one schema
setup failure, one valid model response with provenance gaps, twelve SCALE-Sim
evaluation events, five unique evaluated shapes, a tie against a weak
heuristic, a failed directional explanation, an omitted memory axis, and a
pending accountable decision. It does not establish array optimality, equal
total cost, method parity, physical feasibility, or any full-system XR result.

Neither record produces a win claim. The cache study requires a new fully
retained execution. The array study requires a newly frozen exhaustive
comparison before a broader candidate-selection claim, followed by the
system-relevant checks that its local simulator cannot perform. The next
chapter asks which parts of either study can transfer when the workload,
objective, tool, implementation target, or system context changes
(@sec-loop-patterns-across-stack).
